title: Interfaces and Object Types
summary: Describe the shape of your objects so they stay consistent.
heading: Interfaces and Object Types

blocks.text: Objects (Chapter 7) hold named values. An interface describes the shape an object must have — which properties it needs and what type each one is.

blocks.label: interface

blocks.text: Once you have a shape, you can use it as a type. TypeScript then checks that every object matches it — no missing or misspelled properties.

blocks.label: using it

blocks.text: A ? marks a property as optional. readonly means it can be set once but not changed afterwards.

blocks.label: options

blocks.text: A type alias gives a name to any type. A union (|) lets a value be one of several types — handy for fixed sets of options.

blocks.label: type

blocks.text: Rule of thumb: use interface for object shapes, and type for unions and aliases.

items: Use it as a type so objects must match it.
? makes a property optional; readonly locks it.
type names any type; | builds a union of options.
Interfaces for shapes, types for unions.
